title: Idempotent commands and postings keyed on stable business identifiers
status_rationale: Unbound requirements specify this design but nothing is implemented, operated or tested (unbound@9b38de47). The evidence mechanism, freshness and automation fields describe the target design.
target_answer: Every mutating Unbound command and every posting is idempotent on a stable business key, not a transport retry ID: for example GrantId plus installment, PaymentIntentId, or ScheduleId plus occurrence (UNB-XIN-EVA-005, UNB-RCN-GRT-004). Posting is idempotent per source event ID and accounting book, so at most one original journal exists per pair whatever the posting-rule version (RR-ACC-MDL-007-r1). Each external observation type has a registered key derived from source data (an ACH return is keyed on original trace, return reason code and return trace); a repeat with the same key and payload hash is acknowledged with no effect, while the same key with a different hash is not applied and opens a DuplicateKeyConflict case. Fee runs are idempotent per fund, schedule, period and segment set (RR-ADM-028-r1). Keys are enforced by database unique constraints in the same transaction as the effect, so a race between duplicates cannot produce two effects.
current_practice: Not established. Unbound exists only as requirements (unbound@9b38de47); there is no ledger, payment, workflow or control implementation, no production deployment and no customer. Unknown; no operating evidence located.
intended_practice: Implement an idempotency key registry per command and observation type with unique constraints and payload hashes; contract tests replay every command.

title: External effects: exactly-once internally, at most one live attempt externally
status_rationale: Unbound requirements specify this design but nothing is implemented, operated or tested (unbound@9b38de47). The evidence mechanism, freshness and automation fields describe the target design.
target_answer: Unbound does not claim exactly-once execution at external providers; no local guarantee is represented as provider exactly-once (REQ-X-019). Internally, state changes and the outbound message that will cause an external effect commit in the same transaction through a durable outbox, consumers are idempotent and ordering is per subject (UNB-EVT-002). Every external effect has a durable issuance receipt and external idempotency key so retries, recovery and replay cannot repeat payments, grants, trades, notices or filings (UNB-IMM-006, UNB-DATA-009, UNB-RES-002). Process managers issue commands with stable keys and never hold locks across external calls (UNB-XIN-EVA-007). A payment rail is eligible only if the provider contractually supports idempotent submission and status query (TVR-PAY-002); where a rail lacks an end-to-end key (noted for ACH), reconciliation and the unknown-outcome protocol close the gap. The guarantee offered is at most one live attempt per grant under any failure (TVR-PAY-001).

intended_practice: Implement the transactional outbox and effect-receipt store; select providers only with idempotent submission and status query.

title: Atomic approval, reservation and journal commit
status_rationale: Unbound requirements specify this design but nothing is implemented, operated or tested (unbound@9b38de47). The evidence mechanism, freshness and automation fields describe the target design.
target_answer: Routine grant approval and the currency reservation against net capacity commit atomically in one transaction, so two simultaneous grants that together exceed capacity cannot both succeed and a failed grant has neither approval nor reservation (REQ-X-002, CNV-FIN-001). Every domain fact with a financial effect carries the journal batch or reservation ID committed in the same database transaction, and balances are computed only from insert-only journal and reservation tables (UNB-XIN-EVA-001). Deadline-bearing obligations are persisted in the same transaction as the state change that creates them (UNB-XIN-WFA-001). A batch such as a payment file or recurring-grant run is only a container: each item commits in its own transaction with its own key, and a batch ends PartiallyCompleted with per-item outcomes rather than all-or-nothing ambiguity (UNB-XIN-EVA-011).
current_practice: Not established. Unbound exists only as requirements (unbound@9b38de47); there is no ledger, payment, workflow or control implementation, no production deployment and no customer. Unknown; no operating evidence located.
intended_practice: Keep the authoritative ledger and facts in one PostgreSQL cluster per the architecture so atomicity is a local transaction property, not a distributed protocol (CNV-ARC-001).

title: Concurrency control, serializable reservations and dispatch fencing
status_rationale: Unbound requirements specify this design but nothing is implemented, operated or tested (unbound@9b38de47). The evidence mechanism, freshness and automation fields describe the target design.
target_answer: A grant reservation is created only inside one serializable transaction that computes reservable capacity from the authoritative ledger, reservation and hold records for the fund and every constrained ancestor (pool cash buffer, custody account, entity, restricted sub-balance), acquiring locks in a deterministic order; display projections are never used for this check (RR-UNB-GFUND-021-r1). Concurrent recommendations, redemptions or liquidations cannot commit the same liquidity twice (UNB-GFUND-021, UNB-NAV-028). Conflicting instructions from different advisors move both to HeldConflict unless policy resolves them deterministically (UNB-XIN-EVA-012). At the irreversible dispatch step, the release checks the current hold publication version atomically with authorization using a fencing token, and unknown hold state fails closed (CNV-ARC-003). Cancel-versus-submit races resolve by revision with exactly one winner (TVR-GR-004). Tenant migration never permits two active authoritative writers (UNB-TEN-013).

intended_practice: Test the 12 concurrency schedules and 16 invariants named in REQ-X-019 with deterministic interleavings before release.

title: Completeness and accuracy of inputs from external sources
status_rationale: Unbound requirements specify this design but nothing is implemented, operated or tested (unbound@9b38de47). The evidence mechanism, freshness and automation fields describe the target design.
target_answer: Each external source (bank statements and return files, custodian files, processor reports, IRS exempt-organization extracts, sanctions lists) has an expected-delivery calendar and a completeness watermark; a batch is accepted only when its control totals (record count, amount sum or source trailer) match, and a source behind schedule opens a SourceFeedGapDetected case that holds automated actions depending on that source's freshness while still allowing protective actions (UNB-XIN-EVA-004). External files and webhooks carry retrieval evidence and authenticity checks, and ingestion alone never grants sponsor approval (UNB-EVT-003). Provider callbacks are authenticated and deduplicated on provider and event ID and on a semantic key (RR-REQ-X-083-r1). Raw feeds are preserved and duplicate or out-of-order observations never overwrite prior evidence (CNV-FIN-013, UNB-KNOW-027). Input validation at trust boundaries uses explicit schemas and size limits (SEC-DATA-001).

title: Processing integrity and continuously checked financial invariants
status_rationale: Unbound requirements specify this design but nothing is implemented, operated or tested (unbound@9b38de47). The evidence mechanism, freshness and automation fields describe the target design.
target_answer: Unbound defines its processing integrity commitments as explicit invariants that are continuously checkable: balanced journals, valid dimensions, nonduplicated external effects, reconciled control accounts, authorized allocations, preserved restrictions and no unauthorized negative available balance (UNB-ACC-030; Secure Construction Standard, Financial and business invariants). Outputs are computed only from sealed snapshots so they are complete and reproducible (UNB-XIN-EVA-003). Releases deploy in rings and halt automatically when a ledger balance, outbox backlog, unknown-rate or error-budget check breaches its threshold (UNB-XIN-SAS-003). Every business-significant event produces attributable, tamper-evident evidence (SOC2-002), and a missing expected control heartbeat is itself an exception (SOC2-027). These map to the SOC 2 processing integrity criteria if Echelon elects that category in a future SOC 2 scope.

title: Deterministic replay and projection rebuild without side effects
status_rationale: Unbound requirements specify this design but nothing is implemented, operated or tested (unbound@9b38de47). The evidence mechanism, freshness and automation fields describe the target design.
target_answer: Rebuilding projections from an immutable snapshot or checkpoint plus subsequent events produces the same state as full replay; the snapshot is a cache, never authority (UNB-IMM-005). Replay is deterministic and side-effect-free: posting rules apply once at posting time and are not re-applied, replay locates existing journals by source event and book, and external effects require durable issuance receipts so replay cannot repeat them (UNB-DATA-009, RR-ACC-MDL-007-r1, UNB-XIN-EVA-001). Stored events carry schema versions; authoritative consumers that meet an unknown version stop and quarantine rather than skip (UNB-XIN-EVA-008). Replay and rebuild times are load-tested at defined scales, including a 10x grant surge, before storage technology is finalized (UNB-IMM-010, UNB-ACC-036).

title: Unknown outcome handling for timeouts and ambiguous external results
status_rationale: Unbound requirements specify this design but nothing is implemented, operated or tested (unbound@9b38de47). The evidence mechanism, freshness and automation fields describe the target design.
target_answer: When an external call times out or returns an ambiguous result, the item enters an explicit Unknown state; there is no retry button and no automatic retry (TVR-PAY-001, CNV-PAY-004). Each rail has an UnknownResolutionProtocol: status query by idempotency key at defined intervals, reconciliation against bank statements after the settlement window, and a defined evidence combination before NotReceived may be declared, which requires independent approval and creates a linked reissue chain (UNB-RCN-GRT-008). Before the final aging tier a bank trace or rail status request is made; only items still Unobtainable after 30 days go to two independent approvers who record duplicate-risk acceptance and a recovery plan (CNV-PAY-004). A bulk-Unknown event uses graded evidence and dual-control sampling and never bulk-declares NotReceived without per-item proof (TVR-PAY-007). Reissue after a proven NotSubmitted reuses the original idempotency key (UNB-RCN-WF-001). UIs never show success before authoritative confirmation (INT-006, AIN-014).
